newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK AGREES TO LIMIT MONEY MKT ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK AGREES TO LIMIT MONEY MKT ACCESS.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) on Thursday said it had agreed with large domestic banks to limit access to the non-resident investors to the Czech money market, effective immediately.
CNB board member Ludek Niedermeyer also said that the central bank was closing all access to the Lombard credit facility, also effective immediately.
"The central bank, after discussion with leading (domestic) banks, has decided steps that would restrain non-residents' access to our money market," Niedermeyer told Reuters.
He did not elaborate on the move.
He said that the character of the restriction was temporary and reflected the situation on the foreign exchange market.
"This is not a reaction to events only this morning but to the situation that non-residents are taking big positions on the money market. Basically this is increasing the volatility," he said.
The crown, which has been under pressure for over a week, opened steady at about 2.7 percent on the depreication side of its dollar/mark basket midpoint.

But speculators in London moved in soon afterward, pushing the crown to a record low of -6.4 against basket parity, forcing the central bank to step into the market directly for the third time in a week.

The CNB has been waging a war against investors to keep the crown from crashing since last week when a wave of short-selling pushed the currency to more than five percent below the mid-point of the dollar/mark basket, which the central bank uses to fix the crown's exchange rate daily.
Throughout the week, the central bank has been gradually limiting access to the Lombard facility, after the Lombard rate was raised on Friday to 50 percent from a previous 14 percent.
CNB officials noted that the bank's board was not meeting on Thursday, but would hold its next regular meeting on May 29.
